title: [Roadmap] Overview: BaseHarbor releases and development
author: mcpdev80
body:
## Purpose and current direction

This is the authoritative high-level BaseHarbor roadmap. Detailed acceptance belongs in the linked release/feature issues; delivered history belongs in release notes.

Developer experience first: simple by default, secure by default, explicit when needed. Capabilities, not products. Portable Application Intent remains independent from Docker, Podman, Kubernetes, OpenShift and infrastructure products.

Repository / Application → Inspection → Portable Intent → Environment + Policy → Target and Runtime / Capability / Delivery Providers → Plan / Preflight / Reconcile → Verify → Audit / Evidence.

Runtime, capability, delivery, workload-source adaptation and workspace/Git acquisition remain distinct boundaries. Known failures explain cause and the safest next action (#375).

## Current release sequence

v0.4.23 (#571) and v0.4.24 (#603) are published. Their historical evidence does not qualify the current v0.4.25 candidate.

| Release | Authoritative issue | Scope and main dependencies |
| --- | --- | --- |
| v0.4.25 | #872 | Capability-first contracts, selective services and complete ownership-safe add/remove/re-add lifecycle; shared implementation PR #881 |
| v0.4.26 | #873, #888 | Compact wizard, CLI/JSON/MCP footprint and developer docs; bounded workflow/CI V1 with small PRs and conservative test selection |
| v0.4.27 | #874 | Remote development and onboarding; developer access and profile portability #777 |
| v0.4.28 | #875 | Web Console management and complete developer journeys |
| v0.4.29 | #876 | Host portability: #818, #819–#823; final architecture audit #817; Darwin prerequisite #882, Podman Machine #883, actual macOS runtime evidence #884 |
| v0.4.30 | #904 | Native TLS / justified proxies #902; attack protection baseline and DDoS/operator boundaries #903 |
| v0.4.31 | #174 | Final semantic acceptance; quality completion #862 and no-new-features stability reconciliation before freeze |

All these belong to milestone **v0.4.x** (#427). Release qualification/promotion stays ordered; independent future work may proceed on develop while a candidate is frozen. Quality, safety, ownership, CLI/JSON/MCP parity, bilingual documentation and exact-source evidence are requirements of every release.

Binding product correction from #872: **no migration implementation scope before v1, no developer-supplied Application IDs, no unconditional SQL/Secrets/Identity bundle.** Actual provider footprint follows requested capabilities and genuine dependencies. Preserve shared consumers, data, recovery and security during lifecycle changes. #810 records historical v0.4.23 behavior and does not define the current product.

Later releases consume the accepted foundation; they do not silently redefine contracts. Formal compatibility freeze remains #175, not v0.4.25. Standards-first service bindings/provider catalog #390 remains pre-freeze work.

### Host-platform boundary

#876 is authoritative: Linux and real WSL2 developer local/remote paths; macOS arm64 Dev Local with **both Docker Desktop and Podman Machine**. Native macOS amd64 build/conformance alone does not establish runtime support. VM resource evidence and isolation must describe the actual selected runtime.

Automatic macOS Keychain trust and macOS Dev Remote (#886), and Developer ID signing/notarization (#885), are explicitly unscheduled follow-ups outside v0.4.29. They retain `status/backlog` without an invented release assignment.

### Older open work

Released v0.4.23 tasks #805–#808 and #810–#814 are closed with final qualification/publication links. Earlier bugs #755, #764 and #765 are closed with released implementation/test references.

Keep #750–#752 (inspect), #754 (typed machine preconditions), #766 (orphan cleanup) and #815 (remaining all-stack native startup acceptance) visible until their exact remaining scope has evidence. Age or a published version is not proof of completion. #815's build fixes are delivered; its broader startup requirement must not be silently discarded.

#862 introduces minimal version-pinned static/vulnerability checks and risk-focused coverage as early as practical and ratchets them across releases; final completion belongs to #174. Assessment #887 is review/backlog material, not automatic additional v0.4.25 release scope.

## Later milestones

| Milestone | Parent | Planned children |
| --- | --- | --- |
| v0.5.x | #428 | Formal freeze #175; state versioning/compatibility #297; cross-component contracts #298; upgrade/recovery/deprecation #299; portability acceptance #300 |
| v0.6.x | Reserved | Additional compatible availability extensions only; the original HA foundation was delivered before freeze |
| v0.7.x | #430 | Namespace-first Kubernetes Runtime foundation #102 and #304–#310; delegated delivery / GitOps #325 |
| v0.8.x | #431 | Kubernetes Complete, lifecycle/provider/recovery/observability/DX parity and production acceptance #313–#320 |

No pre-v1 migration obligation is introduced by the compatibility/versioning roadmap. Fundamental Application/Provider boundaries must be settled before formal freeze.

Unscheduled ecosystem work: #100 (operator RBAC/JIT), #181 (air gap/private OCI), #209 (optional ecosystem). These retain `status/backlog`; promoting them requires an explicit scope decision.

## Release and issue workflow

- v0.4.25 alone retains its shared PR #881 and existing procedure. From v0.4.26, #888 governs small task branches/PRs against develop, conservative targeted CI and separately frozen release candidates. Other contributors need @mcpdev80 approval; his own PRs retain a documented solo-maintainer exception with required checks. Preserve others' commits; no force-push over shared work. #882 remains the agreed develop prerequisite exception.
- Release umbrellas own scope, ordering, cross-cutting acceptance and release completion. Focused children reference their parent; do not create duplicate roadmaps or turn every heading into a ticket.
- Use `kind/*` for issue type, `area/*` for affected domains and `status/backlog` only for unscheduled work. Milestones are release series; specific patch assignments live in release/parent issues.
- Issues own future work, specs normative semantics, ADRs rationale and release notes delivered history.
- An issue closes only when its bounded implementation and required evidence are complete. Missing/failed/skipped/unverified acceptance stays open. Reuse green evidence only when the verifier proves unchanged inputs; rerun affected gates.
- Candidate readiness covers BaseHarbor, Demo, Console, Node Connector, CLI/JSON/MCP contracts, EN/DE docs, Pages candidate build/navigation, changelog/release notes, immutable ecosystem pins and release-specific evidence.
- Preparation does not authorize complete pre-release execution, merge, tag, publication or production Pages deployment. Those follow separately authorized release steps.

comments.body:
## Roadmap clarification — v0.4 completion vs v0.5 freeze

The release structure remains:

```
v0.4.x  finish the missing product/runtime/developer primitives
v0.5.x  freeze, version, harden and prove the complete contract
```

### v0.4.x must be complete before the v0.5 freeze track

Concrete implementation gaps currently tracked in #367–#379 must be closed before v0.5:

- trustworthy runtime/workload convergence (#367, #379)
- artifact/image identity sufficient to detect stale/incompatible realized state
- repository capability detection and app-vs-infrastructure classification (#368, #371)
- provider-neutral application intent; e.g. logical SQL capability, while PostgreSQL is the current default provider realization
- guided secrets, concise human summary and complete interactive init (#369, #370, #373, #374)
- human-readable/actionable runtime failures and preflight conflict handling (#375)
- real developer happy-path acceptance plus deterministic CI path (#372)

The normal developer model remains:

```
baha app init
baha up
```

BaseHarbor abstracts operational work but does **not** hide platform facts. Application-relevant capability/provider/runtime versions, compatibility and changes must remain observable through concise human output and detailed verbose/JSON/MCP state.

### v0.5.x is the freeze track

- #175 freezes the public/domain boundaries and inventory.
- #297 versions/migrates BaseHarbor-owned persisted state.
- #298 formalizes cross-component compatibility.
- #299 finalizes upgrade/recovery/deprecation behavior.
- #300 proves portability/compatibility end to end.

v0.5 may finalize/version/harden these semantics; it must not reopen application intent, ownership, provider axes, developer journey, artifact convergence semantics or add a new foundational platform direction.

comments.author: mcpdev80
comments.body:
## Standards-first pre-freeze dependency

#390 is now the single architecture issue for standards-first service contracts, Service Binding alignment, JSON Schema 2020-12, Provider Catalog metadata and service-vs-protocol separation.

Roadmap ordering:

```
current v0.4.x correctness/DX
  -> #390 standards-first contract alignment
  -> #174 semantic full-stack acceptance
  -> v0.5.x freeze/compatibility track
```

#390 does not replace existing provider/capability issues; it fixes the common contract boundary they consume.

comments.author: mcpdev80
comments.body:
## Standards-first pre-freeze alignment

Track the concrete alignment work in #391.

Roadmap rule:
- v0.4.x must finish the standards-first service/binding/provider-catalog boundary.
- v0.5.x freezes, versions, hardens and proves it.

Do not create parallel product-specific contracts. Existing v0.4 capability IDs remain compatible until their mapping/migration is explicit and tested.

comments.body: Roadmap clarification: added #397 as a v0.4.15 companion prerequisite alongside #212. Sequence remains 0.4.15 audit/evidence + TLS/access baseline → 0.4.16 provider SDK → 0.4.17 managed identity/OIDC/MFA/Keycloak → 0.4.18 semantic acceptance → v0.5 freeze.

comments.author: mcpdev80
comments.body: Added pre-v0.5 observability semantic completion issue #398: when Metrics/Logs are enabled, BaseHarbor must automatically collect supported workload and managed-provider signals (including provider audit for PostgreSQL/Valkey/OpenBao/object storage), while disabled intent stays disabled. Workload developer contract is OpenMetrics for metrics and stdout/stderr for logs.
